review.perspective: Evaluate whether the plan delivers the user-requested experience and prevents the same scope/order/accounting failure, beyond matching documents and passing positive structural checks. Challenge counterexamples against actual selection/synchronization gates and mutated planning fixtures. No claim is made about unimplemented product behavior.

findings.finding: Roadmap repair had drifted into product construction before user approval.
findings.resolution: W05 is explicitly blocked, product work is suspended, every product item depends on W05, and approval holds appear in current roadmaps and legacy worker packets.

findings.finding: Generic conversation retention and interaction registration had absorbed action-decision execution machinery.
findings.resolution: W01 owns interaction contracts; W03 owns actual readable turns; W07 owns native proposals, decision contracts/storage, serialized execution and observed receipts.

findings.finding: The construction order required runtime/AG-UI work before basic shell layout, and action mediation could precede native result presentation.
findings.resolution: Shell items precede runtime integration; ordinary Q&A, native Review preflight, replay and actual Work-result routing precede complete action mediation.

findings.finding: Shared examiner slots could be mistaken for complete domain conformance.
findings.resolution: Separate registry construction from native scientific, writing Requirement/Interpretation and unrelated event-planning adapters. The third definition remains a proposal for the user approval decision.

findings.finding: Native examination and Review preflight lacked an explicit prerequisite for exact Source reading.
findings.resolution: Both depend on FE-A1.4-W04; the critical omission fixture now rejects its removal.

findings.finding: Agent graph guidance could precede stale/restricted-result protection.
findings.resolution: Guidance depends on FE-A1.4-W21; the critical omission fixture rejects its removal.

findings.finding: The integrated repeated-cycle workflow could be closed before explicit disposition and selective invalidation owners.
findings.resolution: W13 depends on W14/W15 and recorded graph guidance, and still requires at least two connected actual cycles with scoped criteria and open-obligation limits.

findings.finding: Preparatory failures could escape the broad-diagnosis rule, sustaining local construction loops.
findings.resolution: The proposed policy counts construction/preparatory failures under the same owning item, preserves numbered step evidence and requires a changed remedy after repeated failure.

review.decision_reserved_for_user: Approve or reject the exact proposed scope, including the unrelated event-planning definition. Product implementation remains blocked.
limits: The diagnosis ID descriptions use the recorded repository repair sequence and accepted contracts; they do not claim a verbatim reproduction of an unavailable earlier chat response.
Planning tests establish a reviewable consistent plan and current execution hold; real copilot, examiners, graph cycles and native effects require the future production checks listed under each item.

Legacy worker launch instructions were subordinated by documentation; no controller code was modified to introduce a new software enforcement mechanism. Existing A1 selection and Wave 6/7/8 mutation gates were exercised read-only.

prior_attempts.result: 41 adverse planning checks passed. Manual critical review additionally identified missing Source-reading and graph-fencing dependencies; those were repaired before the final 43-check rerun.
